target_customer: HR and People Operations teams at high growth, Slack based companies
problem: People Ops teams coordinate onboarding, offboarding and other programs manually across people and tools, which is slow and error prone.
product_category: People Operations workflow software in Slack

founders.name: John Wetzel
founders.background_notes: Later led HRIS, performance and engagement products at ChartHop.

founders.name: Alex Hilleary
founders.background_notes: Led sales and marketing; later runs The People Ops Community at ChartHop.

competitors.name: Slack Workflow Builder
competitors.what: Slack's own workflow automation, used for onboarding flows by companies like DocuSign and Noom
competitors.traction_then: used by large customers per a 2020 Slack post

technical_complexity.rationale: Slack app plus workflow engine and HRIS integrations; standard SaaS engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Workflows embedded in team processes add some stickiness, but Slack and HRIS vendors could replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not copied out of existence; ChartHop acquired it in March 2022 to add workflows.

market_need_then: Remote work in 2020 made onboarding and offboarding coordination harder and drove adoption of Slack centered tooling.

branding.domain_note: Used teamgather.co; gather.com was not theirs, and the name collided with Gather.town and others.

brand_strength.rationale: Search results show many unrelated companies named Gather, including a better funded one, and no press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Gather was a six person YC S20 team building Slack native People Ops workflows. It raised a small seed in September 2020 and was acquired by ChartHop in March 2022, with terms undisclosed, giving ChartHop automated workflows. The founders joined ChartHop. This reads as a modest soft landing exit with a small funding footprint rather than a breakout, and the generic name collided with other Gather companies.
notes: teamgather.co redirects to charthop.com (acquired). CB Insights total of about 130K USD across three rounds is a single aggregator figure and unverified; seed from Open Opportunity Fund has no stated amount. A podcast result suggests the founders were in the TinySeed program but I could not confirm it is the same Gather, so not recorded. Competitor evidence is thin: only a dated 2020 Slack post found. Name collision judgment is mine from search results. Success and failure factors are partial judgment.
